bug_E1.description: Elixir multi-clause body-level analyses (slice, complexity, taint, contracts, reaching-defs, dead-stores, resources, explain) only see the bodyless spec head. Plug.Conn.send_resp/1 has clauses at lines 437/439/443/453, with 437 being a bodyless head. find_function_node returned the head, so complexity=1/LOC=1 and slice returned just line 437.
bug_E1.fix: In find_function_node_in_subtree, when an Elixir def matches by name but has no do_block child (bodyless head), remember it as a fallback and continue searching. Return the first body-bearing clause; only fall back to the head if no body-bearing clause exists. Matches what `extract` already does and is the minimal `skip-to-first-body-bearing-clause` semantics per scope guardrails.
bug_E1.scope_note: Per-clause iteration (e.g. slicing line 443 which is in the third clause) is deferred to a future pass. Current fix prevents the worst regression: bodyless-head stubs being treated as the full function.

bug_E2.description: `tldr dead` on /tmp/repos/elixir-plug flagged mix.exs::project/0 and mix.exs::application/0 as possibly_dead. These are Mix build-tool reflection callbacks invoked via the framework's reflection mechanism — they have no explicit caller in project source but are NEVER dead.
bug_E2.fix: Added `file_name == "mix.exs"` to the Elixir branch of is_framework_entry_file in dead.rs. Mix is the canonical Elixir build tool; mix.exs is the manifest file. All public defs in mix.exs (project, application, deps, package, etc.) are reflection entry points — same mechanism that rescues wsgi.py / setup.py / views.py for Python web frameworks.
